$comment: SSOT — declarative registry of connectors. `providers` are the pluggable per-category backends (DNS/secrets/registry/observability): consumed by Go (go:embed, packages/core/categories) for module composition AND by the console codegen (apps/console/scripts/gen-connectors.mjs → lib/connectors/registry.generated.ts) for the Project selectors. `builtin` are the first-class cloud + git connectors (cloud federation / OAuth, handled outside the category module system): catalog rows only — seeded into the `connectors` table but NOT emitted to the TS registry. Both arrays are emitted into lib/db/seed/connectors.generated.sql. Go ignores `builtin`. Adding a pluggable provider = a `providers` row + a Go impl + an OpenTofu module under infra/templates/<module_path> — EXCEPT registry providers, whose only artifact is a dockerconfigjson imagePullSecret the runner seeds post-apply (no module; module_path is ""), because the in-tofu kubernetes provider is host+CA-only on AWS and can't create it. `icon_url` is a path under packages/assets/static (the committed asset SSOT, synced into each app's public/) or null when no mark ships for that connector — null is a DECLARED absence that renders the monogram tile with no request; gen-connectors.mjs FAILS on a path that resolves to no committed file.

fields.label: Registry URL

fields.label: Username

fields.label: Password / Secret

providers.name: DigitalOcean Container Registry
providers.description: Pull images from the DigitalOcean container registry.

fields.label: API Token
fields.help: A DigitalOcean API token with registry read access. Used as both username and password.

providers.name: Scaleway Container Registry
providers.description: Pull images from the Scaleway container registry.

fields.label: Secret Key

fields.label: Registry URL

providers.name: Amazon ECR (cross-account)
providers.description: Pull from an ECR registry in a different AWS account — keyless, no stored key. The cluster mints a short-lived pull token in-cluster from a role the target account trusts.

fields.label: Target AWS Account ID
fields.help: The AWS account that owns the ECR registry (the account the cluster pulls from cross-account).

fields.label: Region
fields.help: The ECR registry region, e.g. us-east-1.

fields.label: Registry Host
fields.help: The registry endpoint, e.g. 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com.

fields.label: Target Role ARN
fields.help: An IAM role in the target account that trusts this cluster's workload identity and grants ECR pull (GetAuthorizationToken + BatchGetImage). You create this in the registry account.

providers.name: Google Artifact Registry (cross-project)
providers.description: Pull from an Artifact Registry repository in a different GCP project — keyless, no stored key. The cluster mints a short-lived token in-cluster from a service account the target project granted reader.

fields.label: Target GCP Project ID
fields.help: The GCP project that owns the Artifact Registry repository.

fields.label: Region
fields.help: The Artifact Registry location, e.g. us-central1.

fields.label: Registry Host
fields.help: The registry endpoint, e.g. us-central1-docker.pkg.dev.

fields.label: Reader Service Account
fields.help: The service account the target project granted roles/artifactregistry.reader on the repository. You grant this in the registry project.

providers.name: Azure Container Registry (cross-subscription)
providers.description: Pull from an ACR in a different Azure subscription — keyless, no stored key. The cluster mints a short-lived token in-cluster from an identity the target ACR granted AcrPull.

fields.label: Target Subscription ID
fields.help: The Azure subscription that owns the ACR.

fields.label: Region
fields.help: The ACR region (optional).

fields.label: Registry Host
fields.help: The registry endpoint, e.g. myregistry.azurecr.io.

fields.label: Pull Identity Client ID
fields.help: The client id of the identity the target ACR granted AcrPull. You grant this in the registry subscription.

fields.label: Password / Token

fields.label: Registry Host

providers.name: Scaleway Container Registry (OCI Helm)

fields.label: Secret Key
fields.help: A Scaleway secret key. The registry username is fixed to 'nologin'.

fields.label: Registry Host
fields.help: Your Scaleway registry host, e.g. rg.fr-par.scw.cloud.

providers.name: Amazon ECR (OCI Helm)
providers.description: Pull Helm charts from a cross-account Amazon ECR registry keylessly — an in-cluster refresher mints + rotates the ~12h ECR token from the connected AWS account (no stored key). Rolling out behind a feature gate.

fields.label: Registry AWS Account ID
fields.help: The AWS account that owns the ECR registry (the cross-account target).

fields.label: Region
fields.help: The ECR region.

fields.label: Registry Host
fields.help: The ECR registry host, e.g. 1234.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com.

fields.label: Target Role ARN
fields.help: The IAM role in the registry account that trusts this cluster's OIDC and grants ECR pull; the in-cluster refresher assumes it to mint the token.

providers.name: Amazon ECR Public (OCI Helm)
providers.description: Pull Helm charts from Amazon ECR Public (public.ecr.aws) keylessly — an in-cluster refresher mints + rotates the public-registry token under the cluster's own identity (no stored key). Rolling out behind a feature gate.

fields.label: Registry Host
fields.help: The ECR Public registry host (defaults to public.ecr.aws).

providers.name: Doppler
providers.description: Manage application secrets in Doppler, an external secrets store.

fields.label: API Token
fields.help: A write-capable Doppler API token (personal or Service-Account). A read-only service token cannot manage secrets.

fields.label: Project
fields.help: The Doppler project the managed secrets live in.

fields.label: Config
fields.help: The Doppler config (environment) within the project.

providers.name: Infisical
providers.description: Manage application secrets in Infisical, an external (SaaS or self-hosted) secrets store.

fields.label: Machine Identity Client ID
fields.help: Infisical Universal Auth (machine identity) client id.

fields.label: Machine Identity Client Secret
fields.help: Infisical Universal Auth client secret.

fields.label: Host
fields.help: Infisical API host (override for self-hosted).

fields.label: Workspace ID
fields.help: The Infisical workspace (project) id, used to provision the secrets.

fields.label: Project Slug
fields.help: The Infisical project slug, used to read the secrets in-cluster. Copy it from the project settings with 'Copy Project Slug' — it is not the workspace id.

fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Environment slug (e.g. dev, staging, prod).

fields.label: Folder Path
fields.help: Secret folder path.

providers.name: 1Password
providers.description: Manage application secrets in 1Password, an external secrets store.

fields.label: Service Account Token
fields.help: A 1Password Service Account token (supports creating items).

fields.label: Vault UUID
fields.help: The 1Password vault UUID the managed secrets live in.

providers.name: Generic (Vault-compatible)
providers.description: Manage application secrets in a Vault-KV-API-compatible endpoint (HashiCorp Vault, OpenBao, or any server exposing the Vault KV v2 HTTP API). Workloads resolve values in-cluster via the External Secrets Operator.

fields.label: Endpoint Address
fields.help: Base URL of the Vault-KV-API-compatible server, e.g. https://secrets.example.com:8200

providers.name: AWS Secrets Manager (cross-account)
providers.description: Read secrets from a Secrets Manager in a different AWS account — keyless, no stored key. The External Secrets Operator assumes a role the target account trusts and reads across the account boundary.

fields.label: Target AWS Account ID
fields.help: The AWS account that owns the Secrets Manager secrets (the account the cluster reads from cross-account).

fields.label: Region
fields.help: The Secrets Manager region, e.g. us-east-1.

fields.label: Target Role ARN
fields.help: An IAM role in the secrets account that trusts this cluster's external-secrets IRSA role and grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue. You create this in the secrets account.

fields.label: External ID
fields.help: Only if the target role's trust policy carries an sts:ExternalId condition — enter the same value you set on the bootstrap module's external_id. Leave blank when it does not; STS rejects the assume when the two disagree.

providers.name: GCP Secret Manager (cross-project)
providers.description: Read secrets from a Secret Manager in a different GCP project — keyless, no stored key. The External Secrets Operator reads the target project with the cluster's Workload Identity, which the target project granted secretAccessor.

fields.label: Target GCP Project ID
fields.help: The GCP project that owns the Secret Manager secrets and granted your cluster's Workload-Identity principal roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor.

fields.label: Region
fields.help: The secret location for regional secrets, e.g. us-central1 (optional; leave blank for global secrets).

providers.name: Azure Key Vault (cross-subscription)
providers.description: Read secrets from a Key Vault in a different Azure subscription (same tenant) — keyless, no stored key. The External Secrets Operator authenticates with the cluster's workload identity, which the target vault granted Key Vault Secrets User.

fields.label: Target Subscription ID
fields.help: The Azure subscription that owns the Key Vault (same tenant as the cluster — cross-tenant is not supported keyless).

fields.label: Key Vault URL
fields.help: The target Key Vault URL, e.g. https://my-vault.vault.azure.net.

providers.name: Alibaba KMS Secrets Manager (cross-account)
providers.description: Read secrets from a KMS Secrets Manager in a different Alibaba RAM account — keyless, no stored key. The External Secrets Operator's RRSA identity assumes a role the target account trusts via its OIDC provider.

fields.label: Target RAM Account ID
fields.help: The Alibaba account that owns the KMS Secrets Manager secrets.

fields.label: Region
fields.help: The KMS region, e.g. cn-hangzhou.

fields.label: Target Role ARN
fields.help: The acs:ram role in the secrets account that trusts this cluster's RRSA OIDC provider and grants KMS secret read. You create this in the secrets account.

fields.label: Target OIDC Provider ARN
fields.help: The RAM OIDC provider in the secrets account trusting this cluster's ACK OIDC issuer. ESO's RRSA exchanges its projected token for the target role via this provider.
